summary: Richard Gombrich is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned his BA and DPhil at the University of Oxford, also studying under K. R. Norman, Walpola Rahula, and Gananath Obeyesekere. He served as Oxford's Boden Professor of Sanskrit (1965–2004).

Richard Hartshorne studied at Princeton University (~1917–1920) and the University of Chicago (~1921–1924). He held posts at the University of Minnesota (~1924–1940) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1945–1970).

Richard Hauschild was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Leipzig, Tübingen, and Jena under Albert Debrunner and Johannes Hertel, earning his PhD (~1926) and Habilitation (1948). He was a lecturer, PD, and professor at the University of Jena (1938–1967).

Richard Henebry was a linguist who studied at St. John's College, Waterford, St Patrick's Pontifical University, Maynooth, and the universities of Greifswald and Freiburg, studying under Heinrich Zimmer (~1895–1898).

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Richard Hugh Robinson studied at the University of Alberta, SOAS, and the University of London under Arthur Waley and David Friedman. He served as professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from 1964 to 1970.

Richard Hughes Seager works in religious and Buddhist studies. Educated in the University of Wisconsin System, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University (PhD ~1987), he served as Associate Professor of Religion at Hamilton College (~1994–2014).

Richard Hönigswald was a philosopher who studied at the universities of Vienna, Halle-Wittenberg, and Graz between ~1894 and ~1906. He later held academic posts at the University of Breslau (1906–1930) and the University of Munich (1930–1933).

Richard J. Davidson studied at New York University (BA 1972) and Harvard University (PhD 1976). He has held multiple posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, becoming a professor in 1987 and serving as director from 2001 to 2017.

Richard Jay Kohn was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1988 under Geshe Lhundup Sopa, and also studied under Lama Tharchin Rinpoche.

Richard K. Payne is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history and archaeology who studied under Chisei Aratano and Taisen Miyata. He served as Dean at the Institute of Buddhist Studies from ~1994 to 2018.

Richard Karl Heinrich von Kienle was an Indo-European linguist who completed his Habilitation under Hermann Güntert at Heidelberg University. He held positions at Heidelberg (from 1934), the University of Hamburg (1941–1946), and the Free University of Berlin (1953–1974).
Richard Keith Sprigg was a linguist and Tibetologist educated at Oakham School (~1936–1940). He held long-term posts at the University of London and SOAS University of London from ~1948 to 1980.

Richard Kieckhefer is a historian and scholar of religious studies who earned his PhD at the University of Texas at Austin (~1972). In 1975, he became a professor of history and religious studies at Northwestern University.

Richard King is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy who earned his PhD from Lancaster University (~1992). He held faculty posts at the University of Stirling, Vanderbilt University (~2002–2011), and the University of Glasgow (~2011–2012).
Richard Kühnau was an Indologist who studied at the University of Breslau from 1878 to 1885, earning his PhD under the instruction of Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Alfred Hillebrandt.

Richard Lionel Spittel was active in Indology and medicine. He completed his LMS at Ceylon Medical College (~1900–1905), joined the National Hospital of Sri Lanka in 1910, and lectured at Ceylon Medical College from ~1910 to 1935.

Indologist Richard Löbbecke studied at Marburg, Göttingen, Berlin, and Leipzig, completing his PhD (~1908) under Ernst Windisch. His other teachers included Bruno Lindner, August Conrady, Franz Kielhorn, Friedrich Carl Andreas, Richard Pischel, Karl Friedrich Geldner, Emil Sieg, and Georg Huth.

Richard M. Jaffe is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He taught at North Carolina State University (~1995–2000) before becoming a Professor of Religious Studies at Duke University, starting around 2000.

Richard Morris was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics educated at Battersea Training College. He served as King's College School Winchester lecturer (1869), Philological Society ex-president (~1874–1875), and Royal Masonic School for Boys headmaster (1875–1888).

Richard O. Meisezahl was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who founded the International Institute for Tibetan and Buddhist Studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Bonn (-1944), where he served as an assistant from 1945 to 1947.
